# `scripts/fp/warmup/`

[Index](index.md)

## `scripts/fp/warmup/render_info.gd`

class_name `RenderInfo` · extends `Node`

Web probe aid (flag web_first_use_marks, web only): every SECONDS prints one console line with what the renderer drew in the last frame of the main viewport, so a Planner or street change shows its effect in objects, primitives and draw calls, separately for the visible pass and the shadow passes. RENDERINFO {"vis":{"obj":..,"prim":..,"draw":..},"shadow":{...},"mode":"orbit"} Never logs anything else; the tag is a fixed literal.

### Constants

- `SECONDS = 3.0`
- `LINE = "RENDERINFO "`

### Functions

- `static func attach(m: Node) -> void`: Adds a RenderInfo under main when the probe marks are on (the web build with the flag), else nothing.
- `func new_materials(cap: int) -> Array[String]`: NEWMAT console lines for up to cap materials that came into the scene since the last call (the first call only learns them): what first shows in the mid-play shader hitches. Kind, a name or path of the material and the node that carries it; nothing player-written.
- `func line() -> String`: The console line for the main viewport as of the last drawn frame.

## `scripts/fp/warmup/shader_warmup.gd`

class_name `ShaderWarmup` · extends `RefCounted`

Shader warm-up for the web build. The Compatibility renderer links each shader program the first time something is drawn with it, and in the browser that wait is synchronous (a median of 37 ms, up to 213 ms, per program): a new material coming into view, the lamps turning on, the Tab overview showing far trees, each stalled the page for several hundred ms in the first minutes of play. run() does that work during the loader veil instead (docs/runbooks/web-probe-kit.md, "Shader warm-up"): it asks WarmCollector for the distinct draws the scene makes (and for a short list of things that are not in it yet but come within the first minutes: people's cut-out materials, a construction beacon, a new building's leaves), parks one tiny copy of each in front of the camera (WarmStage) in the sun's two shadow states, a few per frame with a time budget, so the page stays responsive and the loader can show progress. Off the web it does nothing (the desktop links in the pipeline cache), and so with the flag web_shader_warmup off. BootClock.finish() calls it right after the first frame, so the veil is lifted only when it is done (or its budget is spent: what is left stays lazy, as before).

### Constants

- `FLAG = "web_shader_warmup"`
- `TUNING_PATH = "user://warmup_tuning.json"`
- `REPORT_PREFIX = "WARMUP "`
- `REPORT_VERSION = 1`
- `DEFAULT_BUDGET_MS = 3000.0`: Stop starting batches when the stage has run this long (ms): what is left links in play.
- `FRAME_TARGET_MS = 300.0`: A batch is sized to take about this long (ms) at the last frame's cost per copy. Every frame also draws the whole street (about 25 ms of fixed cost here), so a bigger batch warms more per second; near the end of the budget a batch shrinks to what the rest could pay at COPY_GUESS_MS a copy.
- `MAX_BATCH = 12`
- `COPY_GUESS_MS = 120.0`
- `OVERVIEW_FRAMES = 6`: Frames the overview is held open for the warm-up (its camera eases up over the first few).
- `SLOW_FRAME_MS = 100.0`: A frame over this (ms) is counted in the report as a hitch behind the veil.
- `LARGE_SCENE_RECIPES = 600`: A scene with more recipes than this is not warmed (a grown city: 1,575 against a new city's 190). Every frame of the stage also draws the whole real scene, and the first frame of the shadow-off pass draws all of it again in a new state (1.9 s on a day-10 city): the budget is gone before the pass has warmed anything, so the warm-up only added 0.8 to 2.1 s of boot and removed no hitch (frames over 100 ms 9 and 9, against 9 and 9 without it).

### Properties

- `force: bool`: Tests set this to run on the desktop.
- `veil_check: Callable`: Tests set this to say whether the loader's veil is up (default: WebSupport.veil_up()).
- `report: Dictionary`: The report of the last run ({} before one, and when it did not run).

### Functions

- `static func active() -> bool`: True on the web build (or force) with the flag on.
- `static func tuning() -> Dictionary`: The tunables: defaults, overridden by user://warmup_tuning.json (a probe and test knob: {"budget_ms", "states": ["prototypes", "unlit+noshadow", "orbit", "overview", "lit", "unlit"], "max_recipes", "large_scene_recipes"}).
- `static func run(main: Node) -> void`: Runs the warm-up for the scene under main (needs main.active_camera()). Awaitable; returns when done. Safe to call when inactive: it returns at once.
- `static func render_state(cam: Camera3D, with_lights: bool = true) -> Dictionary`: What the renderer is told about the view the warm-up draws in (which shader families it needs follow from it): the viewport's scaling, the environment's effects and fog mode, the sun, the lights.
- `static func progress_pct(done: int, total: int, elapsed_ms: float, budget_ms: float) -> int`: The loader's percentage: the share of the work done or the share of the budget spent, whichever is further along, so a run that ends on its budget (most of them: a scene has more recipes than 3 s can draw) reaches 100% as the veil lifts, not the share of recipes it got to.

## `scripts/fp/warmup/shadow_hold.gd`

class_name `WarmShadowHold` · extends `RefCounted`

Holds the sun and the fog in another state for the frames of one warm-up state, then puts them back. Each state is a different shader program per material: - "noshadow": the sun without shadows lights a surface in the base pass instead of in the extra sun-shadow pass. It is what the Tab overview draws (the aerial view turns the shadow off) and what dusk and dawn draw while the sun is too weak for one (SkyDirector). - "orbit": four shadow splits and exponential fog, as the Planner view has them (the street has two splits and depth fog): the programs the Planner's first frames used to link in one stall. SkyDirector and the street profile write these every tick, so the hold writes them again just before each frame is drawn. stop() puts the values back.

### Functions

- `func start(p_sun: DirectionalLight3D, p_env: Environment = null, p_kind: String = "noshadow")`
- `func stop() -> void`
- `func is_holding() -> bool`

## `scripts/fp/warmup/warm_collector.gd`

class_name `WarmCollector` · extends `RefCounted`

Finds the draws the scene will make, as a list of recipes, one per distinct material: a material on a plain mesh, on a MultiMesh (with or without per-instance colours and custom data), casting shadows or not, is one recipe, whatever meshes carry it. Instances with the same combination link the same shader programs, so the warm-up (ShaderWarmup) draws one tiny copy of each under the loader veil and the browser links its programs then, instead of in the middle of play. One material to a recipe keeps a batch's cost small and its order meaningful (a building with thirty materials is thirty recipes, not one frame of two seconds). Read-only: nothing under the root is touched. A skinned mesh counts like any other: the skeleton is its own pass, and the scene program that draws it is the plain mesh's for that material.

### Constants

- `PROTOTYPES_PATH = "res://data/warm_prototypes.json"`: Where the list of things to warm that are not in the scene yet lives.

### Functions

- `static func collect(root: Node, near: Vector3 = Vector3.ZERO, cap: int = 2000, skip: Array = []) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Recipes under root, nearest to near first (the order the warm-up draws them), at most cap. Nodes named in skip (and everything below them) are left out: the warm-up's own stage.
- `static func prototypes(extra: Array[Node3D] = []) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Recipes for the materials and models named in data/warm_prototypes.json (a path that is not there is skipped), then for the nodes in extra (prototypes the features build; freed here).

## `scripts/fp/warmup/warm_stage.gd`

class_name `WarmStage` · extends `Node3D`

The warm-up's stage: a Node3D parked a few metres in front of the active camera that holds one tiny copy of each recipe (WarmCollector) for a frame. The copies draw in the real viewport, with the real sun, fog and environment, so the browser links exactly the shader programs the real instances will want later. Two throwaway lights (an omni and a spot, near-zero energy, no shadows) switch on or off to cover both lighting families: an instance near a lamp is drawn with the omni and spot loops in its shader, one far from every lamp without them, and each is its own program. Everything here is invisible behind the loader veil and freed afterwards.

### Constants

- `DEPTH = 3.0`: Metres in front of the camera, and the size every copy is shrunk to (its mesh keeps the shape).
- `SCALE = 0.01`
- `COLUMNS = 8`: Copies per row of the grid, and the gap between them (metres, before the camera looks at them).
- `GAP = 0.05`
- `LIGHT_ENERGY = 0.02`

### Properties

- `count: int`: Copies alive now.

### Functions

- `func attach(cam: Camera3D) -> void`: Parks the stage in front of camera cam (a child of it, so it follows the camera).
- `func set_lit(on: bool) -> void`: true: the lamps are on (omni and spot loops in the shaders); false: no lamp reaches the copies.
- `func show_batch(batch: Array[Dictionary]) -> int`: Adds a copy of every recipe in batch; they draw in the next frame. Returns how many were made.
- `func clear_batch() -> void`: Frees every copy (the lights stay).
